response.explanation: At line 4, src/presentation/server.ts imports ClubBookingRepository straight from the persistence layer. FF-S03 flags this because a presentation module reaches persistence without going through the business layer. The code shows how the import is used: server.ts is the process entry point and acts as the composition root. It creates the repository once (line 29) and passes that one instance into SessionService (line 30) and ClubBookingService (lines 31-34). Only the business services reach createApp (lines 47-55), so no request-handling code calls the repository directly. The same file imports many other persistence classes the same way (lines 1-3, 6, 9-10), so this edge is one case of a wider wiring pattern rather than a stray shortcut. Still, the presentation layer now depends at compile time on a concrete persistence class, and that skip is what the layering rule forbids. The finding stays a blocking fail. Because this is wiring code and not a data-access path, the fix is structural: move object construction into a separate bootstrap or composition module that the layering rules allow, or have the business layer provide factories. The handler logic does not need to change. No docs, ADRs or comments came with this finding, so no project intent or exception can be cited.
